entities.summary: Bulstrode Whitelocke was an English lawyer, writer, parliamentarian, and one of the commissioners of the Great Seal during the Interregnum. Born into a prominent family, Whitelocke's early education was at Westminster School and later at Christ Church, Oxford. In 1621, he began his legal career, becoming a barrister and later a queen's counsel. During the English Civil War, Whitelocke's family was forced to flee England due to their perceived Royalist sympathies. After the execution of King Charles I in 1649, Whitelocke became a prominent figure in the Parliamentarian faction. He was elected to the House of Commons and served as a member of the Council of State. In 1653, he was appointed as one of the commissioners of the Great Seal, responsible for the formalities of state. Whitelocke's contributions to the development of the English common law and his role in shaping the English constitution have had a lasting impact on the country's legal system. He was knighted in 1660 for his services and died on July 28, 1675. As a chronicler of English history, Whitelocke's works, such as 'A Memorial of the Reign of King Charles the First', offer valuable insights into the tumultuous period of the English Civil War and the Interregnum.
